introduction: On this Sunday, Isaiah sings of God's vineyard, which he tended with love but which yielded only wild grapes. In the Gospel, Jesus tells the parable of tenants who refuse to give the owner his share of the harvest and kill his son. Paul tells us not to be anxious about anything, but to bring everything to God in prayer. Let us bear the fruit that God looks for.

prayerOfTheFaithful.invitation: Brothers and sisters, the Lord has planted us as his vineyard. Let us bring him our prayers.
intentions: For the Church, the vineyard of the Lord: that she may bear fruit of justice and holiness. Let us pray to the Lord.
For those entrusted with responsibility: that they may serve faithfully and give God what is his. Let us pray to the Lord.
For prophets and messengers who are rejected: that God may protect them. Let us pray to the Lord.
For those who are anxious: that the peace of God may guard their hearts and minds. Let us pray to the Lord.
For ourselves: that we may think about whatever is true, honorable, just, pure and lovely. Let us pray to the Lord.
prayerOfTheFaithful.conclusion: Lord God, you have planted us as your vineyard and sent your Son to us. Make us fruitful in good works, and keep our hearts in your peace. Through Christ our Lord.

reflection.title: The vineyard
reflection.body:
Isaiah sings a love song about a vineyard. The owner does everything for it: he clears the stones, plants the best vines, builds a tower and a wine press. "He looked for it to yield grapes, but it yielded wild grapes." Then the prophet reveals the meaning: "For the vineyard of the LORD of Armies is the house of Israel." God looked for justice and found oppression.

In the Gospel, Jesus takes up this image. A landowner plants a vineyard with the same care and leases it to tenants. At harvest time, he sends servants to collect his share of the fruit, but the tenants beat one, kill another, and stone a third. He sends more servants, and they are treated the same way. Finally he sends his son: "They will respect my son." But the tenants say, "This is the heir. Come, let's kill him and seize his inheritance." They throw him out of the vineyard and kill him.

Jesus is telling the story of his own rejection. He is the Son sent by the Father. And he quotes the psalm: "The stone which the builders rejected was made the head of the corner." What people throw away, God makes the foundation.

The parable also speaks to us. We too have been given a vineyard: our lives, our gifts, our faith, the Church, the earth. God expects fruit: justice, love, holiness. The danger is to act as if the vineyard belonged to us.

Paul gives practical advice for living fruitfully: "In nothing be anxious, but in everything, by prayer and petition with thanksgiving, let your requests be made known to God." And: "whatever things are true, whatever things are honorable, whatever things are just, whatever things are pure... think about these things."

This week, ask yourself what fruit God is looking for in your life, and offer him one concrete act of justice or kindness. And bring your anxieties to God in prayer.
